clue.text: Clue to get her love as there's no more Mr Nice Guy!

definitions.text: there's no more Mr Nice Guy

parts.words: there's no more Mr Nice Guy
parts.note: the straight half: the moment when politeness is dropped and a fight starts in earnest

parts.words: Clue to get her love as
parts.note: the other half says the answer is itself a clue: read as wordplay, its last word tells you to rearrange the letters of its first three words, and they spell out the phrase quoted here

explanation.surface: A lovelorn man is told that being nice will not win her, and he should toughen up.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters call this a reverse anagram: the answer is the wordplay and the clue's phrase is the result. THE GLOVES ARE rearranges to GET HER LOVE AS, with OFF as the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers fight bare-fisted when protective padding is removed, so the idiom means hostilities are now open and ruthless.

clue.text: Appropriate opinion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to seize something for yourself
second meaning: a noun, someone's view or angle on a subject

explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective meaning suitable, but here it is the verb, stressed on the last syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something is to seize it, and a person's take on an issue is their personal view.

clue.text: Award in principle for Ezra Pound poem discovered in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so everything assembled is read backwards
dis-covered means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters are taken away
a pun on principal: the principal or leading letter of the next word is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of the poet's first name
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
a sonnet is a fourteen-line poem

explanation.surface: A literary prize given, in theory, for a poem by Ezra Pound that turned up after he retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ezra Pound' looks like one name but splits into two jobs: the poet's initial and the weight abbreviation. 'Award' is a verb here, to honour with a title.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to confer a title of nobility upon them, an honour bestowed as a reward.

clue.text: Insolence of one breaking record

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing vinyl record
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Somebody cheekily smashing a record, or an athlete brazenly beating one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip is informal for cheeky backchat, as in 'less of your lip', which is impudent talk.

clue.text: Discontented veggie student organisation following party line about meat-eater?

indicators.note: with its contents removed, only the outside letters of the word remain

parts.note: just the first and last letters
the NUS is the UK's National Union of Students
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the preceding words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A disgruntled vegetarian students' group angry at a party line on carnivores.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTY and L are read backwards to give LYTRAP. The question mark flags that the meat-eater is a plant, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This carnivorous plant snaps its hinged leaves shut on insects and digests them, so it is a flesh-eater of sorts.

clue.text: Food provided if son has a practice on drums

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for son
taken as written
usage is a customary practice
a roll is a rapid beating on a drum

explanation.surface: A parent promising treats as long as their boy keeps up his drumming practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' means placed after in this down answer: the drums come below the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausage rolls are British pastry snacks, seasoned meat wrapped in flaky crust, eaten at parties and picnics.

clue.text: In seconds archaeologist just unearthed historic scroll of ancient characters

indicators.note: seconds here are the second letters of each word that follows, not units of time

parts.note: the second letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A dig where an archaeologist quickly uncovers an old scroll covered in strange letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes are the letters of old Germanic and Norse alphabets, so runic writing uses those ancient characters.

clue.text: Writer covering five out of six balls ultimately annoys some cricketers

indicators.note: covering for someone means standing in for them, so one piece takes the place of another

parts.note: in cricket an over is six deliveries from one bowler
V is the Roman numeral for five
a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word just before it

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A cricket writer complains that the last ball of the over irritates the batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: PEN replaces V in OVER to give OPENER. Openers are the two batsmen who start a cricket innings.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening pair go in first to bat, so they are a particular kind of cricket player.

clue.text: Trump, taking on complete fool, loses control

indicators.note: taking something on means taking it in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: trump is British slang for breaking wind
complete means all, the whole
a sap is a gullible person

explanation.surface: A jibe at Donald Trump hiring an idiot and then losing his grip.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes it look like the president; in British slang to trump is to break wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who falls apart collapses emotionally and can no longer keep a grip on themselves.

clue.text: For one Falkland Islander, family doctor means gout isn't treated regularly

parts.note: kin are relatives
a GP is a general practitioner, the British family doctor

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter is used

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A Falklands resident hears from the doctor that the gout is going untreated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falkland Islander' suggests a person, but it is a bird living on the islands; 'means' looks like a link but its letters are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: King penguins breed on the Falklands, so one is an example of a native of those South Atlantic islands.

clue.text: One likely to wriggle out of terms of eurozone trade deal

indicators.note: terms are ends or limits, so each word's closing letter is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A slippery negotiator expected to escape the conditions of a European trade agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terms' looks like the conditions of the deal, but it means the words' end points.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a long snakelike fish famous for squirming free, which is why slippery people are compared to one.

clue.text: Grave robbers barely shock bystanders in reconstruction

indicators.note: reconstructing something builds it again in a different arrangement
laid bare, the word is stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: taken as written, then stripped
taken as written

explanation.surface: Onlookers are hardly troubled as cemetery thieves are reenacted.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOCK without its first and last letters leaves HOC, which joins BYSTANDERS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Body snatchers dug up fresh corpses from graveyards to sell to anatomy schools, notoriously in nineteenth-century Britain.

clue.text: Measures small deer pens

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as livestock are shut in a fold

parts.note: does are female deer
s is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Instructions for sizing enclosures for little deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' looks like a noun for enclosures, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A dose is a measured quantity of medicine to be taken at one time.

clue.text: It could be Albert Einstein's conclusion after putting guard on strong spiced tea

parts.note: a watch is a guard keeping lookout
chai is Indian tea brewed with spices

indicators.note: a conclusion is an ending, so the final letter of that name is used

parts.note: the final letter of the physicist's surname

explanation.surface: Albert Einstein reaching a conclusion over a cup of strong chai.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Albert' looks like Einstein's first name, but an albert is a kind of chain for a pocket watch, named after Prince Albert.
explanation.definitionFit: An albert is a heavy chain fastening a pocket watch to a waistcoat buttonhole, so it is one example of this accessory.

clue.text: A guy free from anxiety

parts.note: taken as written
to guy someone is to mock or rib them

explanation.surface: Describing a laid-back man who has no worries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a noun for a man, but it is the verb meaning to make fun of.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at ease is relaxed and comfortable, without nerves or worry troubling them.

clue.text: Presents to eat and drink after work for …

indicators.note: after places the piece named before it in second position, behind the one named next

parts.note: to serve is to work for someone
to sup is to sip a drink

explanation.surface: Laying on food and drinks for people after their working day, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink comes after the work in the answer. The trailing dots join this clue to the next one, but only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve up a meal is to put food on plates and present it to diners.

clue.text: Spot odds on finishing in Derby

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds when a race begins

indicators.note: finishing points to the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A punter checking the odds on horses as they finish the Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's most famous flat horse race, run at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: To spy something is to catch sight of it, the same as spotting it.

clue.text: Pop in lead for Vodafone's current model

indicators.note: the lead of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: the company name's opening letter
the apostrophe-s read as the contraction of is
I is the symbol for electric current
the Model T was Ford's famous early car

explanation.surface: An advert line about the latest mobile phone handset from Vodafone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current model' reads as the newest phone, but current is electrical and the model is a car; the apostrophe-s is the short form of is.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop in is to drop by briefly, which is making a short call on someone.

clue.text: … girl provided in empty company pigeonhole

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed inside the word that follows
an empty word has lost its inside, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: just the first and last letters
a lass is a girl
provided that means if

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: food served to a girl, if an empty firm will slot her in.
explanation.definitionFit: To pigeonhole something is to put it in a category, just as letters are sorted into compartments.

clue.text: Make accusation in article describing artist wearing outfit

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw around something, so this piece encloses the rest

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: someone wearing clothes sits inside them

parts.note: a rig is a set of clothes
an RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece portraying a painter in fancy dress, pointing a finger at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Two wrappings nest here: the outfit is worn around the artist, and the article draws around both. RA, Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to formally charge a person in court, calling them to answer an indictment.

clue.text: See 4
Heard you are joining American TV show — one that gets a lot of interest

definitions.text: one that gets a lot of interest

parts.note: US is short for American, as in US citizen

indicators.note: heard means we want the sound of the words, not their spelling

parts.note: the two words spoken quickly sound like two letters, as in text speak
ER is the American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: Someone tells you that you are joining a US television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets a lot of interest' sounds like popularity, but it means charging high interest on loans.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at extortionate rates of interest, so the lender collects plenty.

clue.text: Consider relaxation to protect muscle

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: rest is relaxation
pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: Advice to think about resting so as not to injure a muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect is to regard or take into account, as in 'with respect to'; similarly consider means to regard.

clue.text: Supply starchy bread containing zero sugars for example

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece sits within the other
read as supple-y, meaning bendily, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
O looks like the number zero

explanation.surface: A bakery supplying starchy loaves that contain no sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is not to provide but the adverb from supple, flexibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugars are one class of these nutrients, alongside starches and fibre, so they are an example.

clue.text: Best Oscars hosts quoted every now and then

indicators.note: a host has others inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Oscar is the radio alphabet word for O, and there are two

indicators.note: now and then means at intervals, so only alternate letters are used

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: The best Academy Awards presenters being quoted from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective for the hosts, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To best a rival is to beat them, and to outdo them is to surpass their efforts.

clue.text: See 5
Advantage of university supporting student through extra writing

indicators.note: going through something means passing inside it

parts.note: a PS, postscript, is text added after a letter

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporter sits underneath what it holds up

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: The benefit of a university that helps a student through extra coursework.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is a positive point in favour of something, a benefit or merit.

clue.text: Cinema lift's controls say G

definitions.note: Ali G is a full name; the answer is the forename that precedes G

indicators.note: the phrase contains, or holds within it, the letters wanted

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: The buttons in a cinema's elevator, with G for the ground floor.
explanation.walkthrough: G looks like the ground-floor button, but Ali G is Sacha Baron Cohen's comic character; 'say' marks the name as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacha Baron Cohen's fake interviewer character is called Ali G, so this forename completes that comedy persona.

clue.text: Case of animal lust — tell her to go wild?

indicators.note: going wild means running out of control, so the letters break out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to tell a woman about one's animal passion and let her run wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal lust' reads as one phrase, but 'animal' ends the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell is the hard protective casing a tortoise or turtle carries on its back.

clue.text: Date of main broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on the air, so we want the sound of the word

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open ocean

explanation.surface: The date of a principal television transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for the high seas.
explanation.definitionFit: To be seeing someone is to be going out with them romantically, which is dating.

clue.text: News about old soldiers buried in manure is crazy

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round another

parts.note: news read as two n's, N being short for new
o is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: something buried lies inside what covers it

parts.note: compost is rotted organic matter used as fertiliser
soldiers are men in the ranks
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gruesome news report of old soldiers buried in a dung heap, judged insane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like a link word, but it supplies the final two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin legal phrase means not of sound mind, describing someone mentally unfit.
